text: The step is a signal-driven step of AssetDisposalWorkflow on task queue rwb-asset in namespace rwb-recovery: it starts when the parent CaseWorkflow forwards the case signal for a case in EVICTION_REQUIRED with POSSESSION_TAKEN, in TITLE_BLOCKED with TITLE_CLEARED, or in ASSET_HELD with READY_TO_SELL, and it owns no Temporal Schedule, no Quartz row, no published event and no consumed subscription.
why: Legacy AC1 gives the trigger only as its trigger, FSD S5 A2.10.2 allows any of a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer while A2.10.4.4 declares no background event, TSD S5 T5.3 gives one published event and no consumed event, and Architecture v5 slide 13 puts an E in the S5 row under S4 without naming the event, so no event name and no Schedule can be written without inventing one.

text: The five consumed reads of this key - the rwb-source-data asset product, the rwb-source-data COLLINS score product, the rwb-case state read, the rwb-case case-move answer and the rwb-decision package read - are treated as class C dependencies even though both metadata rows carry None, the ACE facts are taken on the owner's contracts because the service holds no v_ace_* grant, and the asset row is read as S5's although the Ownership Map lists only asset_sale and listing.
